records.source: בֶּן־שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ יֹאָ֣שׁ בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ צִבְיָ֖ה מִבְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃
records.gloss: [A] son of seven years [was] Joash when he became king, and forty years he reigned in Jerusalem, and [the] name of his mother [was] Zibiah from Beersheba.
pieces: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah from Beersheba.

L.1: A son of seven years [was] Joash when he became king, and forty years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Zibiah from Beersheba.

R.1: Joash was seven years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother was Zibiah from Beersheba.

decisions.choice: the same opening as 2 Kings 12:1-2, without the date by Jehu's reign
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 12:1-2 gives the king's age, the date by the reign of Jehu king of Israel, the length of his reign and his mother's name. Chronicles keeps all of this except the date by the northern king, as it usually does, since it follows the kings of Judah only. It also uses the shorter form of the name, Joash, where Kings mostly has Jehoash; both name the same king, son of Ahaziah (22:11).

decisions.choice: a son of seven years: seven years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being the son of so many years. Joash had been hidden in the house of God for six years while Athaliah ruled, and Jehoiada made him king in the seventh (22:12; 23:1, 11).

decisions.choice: his mother's name: the queen mother named in the formula
decisions.reason: For the kings of Judah the formula names the king's mother, who held a place of her own at court (2 Kings 12:2). Beersheba lay in the far south of Judah.

decisions.choice: Joash was seven years old; Readable in short sentences
decisions.reason: Wording as at 2 Kings 12:1-2, with the name Chronicles uses. Balanced and Readable give the age as English does; Readable splits the formula into short sentences.

records.heading: Joash repairs the temple

records.source: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יוֹאָ֛שׁ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כָּל־יְמֵ֖י יְהוֹיָדָ֥ע הַכֹּהֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And did Joash the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh all [the] days of Jehoiada the priest.
pieces: Joash did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the days of Jehoiada the priest.

L.2: And Joash did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the days of Jehoiada the priest.

R.2: Joash did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right as long as Jehoiada the priest lived.

decisions.choice: all the days of Jehoiada the priest: only while Jehoiada lived
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 12:3 says Jehoash did right "all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him", words that can be read either way. Chronicles is plain: the good verdict covers only the years of Jehoiada's life. After Jehoiada's death the king turns away (verses 17-22). Chronicles also leaves out the note of 2 Kings 12:4 that the high places were not removed.

decisions.choice: did what was right in Yahweh's eyes: the good verdict
decisions.reason: This is the verdict given to kings of Judah who were faithful to Yahweh (14:1; 20:32). Here it is tied to one man's life, and the rest of the chapter shows what happens when that support is gone.

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The good verdict is worded the same way at each level throughout these books.

decisions.choice: as long as Jehoiada the priest lived
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "all the days of Jehoiada" means (m1).

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂא־ל֥וֹ יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע נָשִׁ֣ים שְׁתָּ֑יִם וַיּ֖וֹלֶד בָּנִ֥ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And took for him Jehoiada wives two, and he begot sons and daughters.
pieces: Jehoiada chose two wives for him, and he became the father of sons and daughters.

L.3: And Jehoiada took for him two wives, and he fathered sons and daughters.

R.3: Jehoiada found two wives for Joash, and Joash had sons and daughters.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada took two wives for Joash, and Joash fathered the children
decisions.reason: "For him" is the young king, the subject of the verses before and after. Jehoiada, who had raised him, arranged his marriages, as a father would. The one who "fathered sons and daughters" is Joash.

decisions.choice: sons and daughters: the royal line of David restored
decisions.reason: Athaliah had tried to destroy every member of the royal family, and Joash alone was saved (22:10-11). Chronicles shows the line of David built up again through his children, as Yahweh had promised it would last (21:7; 23:3). His son Amaziah reigns after him (verse 27).

decisions.choice: chose ... for him; found two wives for Joash, and Joash had
decisions.reason: Balanced says "chose" for "took", since Jehoiada did not marry them himself. Readable names Joash twice so that "he" is not taken as Jehoiada (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֖י אַחֲרֵי כֵ֑ןהָיָה֙ עִם־לֵ֣ב יוֹאָ֔שׁ לְחַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was after so, it was with [the] heart of Joash to renew the house of Yahweh.
pieces: Some time later Joash set his heart on restoring the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: And it was after this, it was with the heart of Joash to renew the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: Some time later Joash decided to repair the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: it was with the heart of Joash: Joash set his mind on it
decisions.reason: Something is "with the heart" of a person when he purposes or wants to do it, as with David's wish to build the temple (1 Chronicles 22:7; 28:2).

decisions.choice: renew: restore, put back in good order
decisions.reason: The verb means to make new. Here it is restoring a building that had been damaged and neglected (verse 7); verse 12 uses it beside "repair".

decisions.choice: the temple of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "the house of Yahweh" throughout this chapter, as 2 Kings 12 does; Literal and Balanced keep "house".

records.source: וַיִּקְבֹּץ֮ אֶת־הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּם֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֡ם צְא֣וּ לְעָרֵ֪י יְהוּדָ֟ה וְקִבְצוּ֩ מִכָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל כֶּ֜סֶף לְחַזֵּ֣ק׀אֶת־בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֗ם מִדֵּ֤י שָׁנָה֙ בְּשָׁנָ֔ה וְאַתֶּ֖ם תְּמַהֲר֣וּ לַדָּבָ֑ר וְלֹ֥א מִֽהֲר֖וּ הַֽלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, go out to [the] cities of Judah and gather from all Israel money to repair [the] house of your God from [the] sufficiency of year in year, and you, you shall hurry in the matter; and not hurried the Levites.
pieces: He called the priests and the Levites together and told them, "Go out to the towns of Judah and collect money from all Israel to repair the house of your God, year by year. Do it quickly." But the Levites did not act quickly.

L.5: And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah and gather from all Israel money to repair the house of your God year by year, and you, you shall hurry in the matter." But the Levites did not hurry.

R.5: He called together the priests and the Levites and told them, "Go out to the towns of Judah. Collect money from all the people of Israel every year to repair the temple of your God. Do it soon." But the Levites were in no hurry.

decisions.choice: year by year: as much as is due each year
decisions.reason: The phrase is "from the sufficiency of a year in a year", that is, as often or as much as each year requires. It points to a yearly payment, which verse 6 calls the tax of Moses.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the people of Judah as the whole people of God
decisions.reason: The collectors go to the cities of Judah, yet they gather from "all Israel". Chronicles often calls the people of the southern kingdom "Israel", the heirs of the whole nation (12:1; 23:2).

decisions.choice: you shall hurry ... and the Levites did not hurry: the order and its neglect
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: the king tells them to act quickly, and the narrator says at once that the Levites did not. The repeated word sets up the king's complaint in verse 6. 2 Kings 12:7 says the same of the priests.

decisions.choice: act quickly / Do it quickly; Do it soon / in no hurry
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the two uses of the verb close in wording (m3) while making the command sound natural.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֣א הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ לִֽיהוֹיָדָ֣ע הָרֹאשׁ֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ מַדּ֨וּעַ֙ לֹֽא־דָרַ֣שְׁתָּ עַל־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְהָבִ֞יא מִֽיהוּדָ֣ה וּמִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶת־מַשְׂאַת֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֔ה וְהַקָּהָ֖ל לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְאֹ֖הֶל הָעֵדֽוּת׃
records.gloss: And called the king for Jehoiada the head and said to him, why not have you required on the Levites to bring from Judah and from Jerusalem [the] tax of Moses [the] slave of Yahweh and the assembly of Israel for [the] tent of the testimony?
pieces: So the king summoned Jehoiada the chief priest and said to him, "Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax for the tent of the testimony, which Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the assembly of Israel laid down?"

L.6: And the king called for Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why have you not required of the Levites to bring in from Judah and from Jerusalem the tax of Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and [of] the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?"

R.6: So the king called for Jehoiada the chief priest. He asked him, "Why have you not made the Levites bring in the tax from Judah and Jerusalem? Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the assembly of Israel set this tax for the tent where the covenant tablets were kept."

decisions.choice: the tax of Moses: the half-shekel for the tent of meeting (Exodus 30:12-16)
decisions.reason: When the people were counted in the wilderness, each one paid half a shekel as a ransom for his life, and Moses was to give the money for the service of the tent of meeting (Exodus 30:12-16; 38:25-26). The king treats this as a standing duty that should now pay for the temple. 2 Kings 12:5 speaks of the same money as the money of those who are counted.

decisions.choice: the tax set by Moses and by the assembly of Israel
alternatives: the tax Moses laid on the assembly of Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "Moses" and "the assembly of Israel" to the one word "tax". Read most simply, both stand behind it: Moses commanded it and the assembly accepted it. It can also be read as the tax Moses laid on the assembly, as verse 9 says he laid it "on Israel". The sense of the king's complaint is the same either way.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada the chief: the chief priest
decisions.reason: "The head" is short for the head priest, the title given in verse 11 ("the chief priest"). The king calls Jehoiada to account as the one over the priests and Levites.

decisions.choice: the tent of the testimony: the tabernacle, where the covenant tablets were kept
decisions.reason: The tent is named after the "testimony", the tablets of the covenant kept in the ark (Numbers 9:15; 17:22-23). The king links the temple of his day to the tent of Moses.

decisions.choice: slave of the LORD (Literal); servant of the LORD (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for "Moses the servant of Yahweh" in these books.

decisions.choice: the chief priest
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "priest" to "chief" (m3). Readable explains the tent as Numbers does and splits the question into a question and a statement.

records.source: כִּ֤י עֲתַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ הַמִּרְשַׁ֔עַת בָּנֶ֥יהָ פָרְצ֖וּ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְגַם֙ כָּל־קָדְשֵׁ֣י בֵית־יְהוָ֔ה עָשׂ֖וּ לַבְּעָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: For Athaliah the wickedness, her sons broke into the house of God, and also all [the] holy things of [the] house of Yahweh they made for the Baals.
pieces: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of God and had even used all the holy things of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for the Baals.

L.7: For Athaliah, the wicked woman, her sons broke into the house of God, and also all the holy things of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they made for the Baals.

R.7: The temple needed repairs because the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into God's temple. They had even taken the holy things from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and used them to worship the Baals.

decisions.choice: the wickedness: the wicked woman
decisions.reason: The word is an abstract noun, "wickedness", used of Athaliah herself: she is wickedness in person. It is found only here.

decisions.choice: her sons: her own sons, or those who followed her
decisions.reason: Athaliah's sons by Jehoram had been killed or carried off (21:17; 22:1), except Ahaziah, who reigned briefly (22:2-9). "Her sons" may mean them, in the years before, or more widely her followers and the priests of her Baal worship (23:17). The text does not say more.

decisions.choice: the holy things used for the Baals
decisions.reason: The holy things are the gifts and vessels set apart for Yahweh in the temple. They had been taken for the worship of Baal, whose temple in Jerusalem the people tore down when Athaliah fell (23:17). The plural "Baals" names the Baal gods and their images.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the repairs were needed
decisions.reason: The verse explains why the house needed the king's repairs (verses 4-5), not why the Levites were slow.

decisions.choice: The temple needed repairs because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "for" connects to (m4) and splits the verse into two sentences.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ אֲר֣וֹן אֶחָ֑ד וַֽיִּתְּנֻ֛הוּ בְּשַׁ֥עַר בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה חֽוּצָה׃
records.gloss: And said the king, and they made a chest one, and they put it in [the] gate of [the] house of Yahweh outside.
pieces: At the king's command they made a chest and placed it at the gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, on the outside.

L.8: And the king spoke, and they made one chest and put it at the gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, outside.

R.8: The king gave an order, and they made a chest. They set it outside, at the gate of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the chest at the gate, outside: differs from 2 Kings 12:10
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 12:10 Jehoiada the priest takes a chest, bores a hole in its lid and sets it beside the altar on the right as one enters. Here the king orders it, and it is set outside, at the gate. The two accounts may describe different stages or places, or each tells what matters to it: Kings the priest's part, Chronicles the king's order and the people's free giving at the gate (verse 10).

decisions.choice: a chest: a box for the money
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the ark of the covenant and for a coffin (Genesis 50:26); here it is a plain box for gifts.

decisions.choice: the king said: the king gave the order
decisions.reason: "Said" is often used of a king's command, which others carry out.

decisions.choice: At the king's command; The king gave an order
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the king's word was (m3).

records.source: וַיִּתְּנוּ־ק֞וֹל בִּֽיהוּדָ֣ה וּבִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם לְהָבִ֤יא לַֽיהוָה֙ מַשְׂאַ֞ת מֹשֶׁ֧ה עֶֽבֶד־הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And they gave a voice in Judah and in Jerusalem to bring to Yahweh [the] tax of Moses [the] slave of God on Israel in the wilderness.
pieces: A proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem that the people should bring to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the tax that Moses the servant of God had laid on Israel in the wilderness.

L.9: And they gave a voice in Judah and in Jerusalem to bring to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the tax of Moses the slave of God [laid] on Israel in the wilderness.

R.9: Then a message was sent all through Judah and Jerusalem. It told the people to bring to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the tax that Moses the servant of God had set for Israel in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: gave a voice: made a proclamation
decisions.reason: To "give a voice" or "pass a voice" is to have something announced publicly (30:5; 36:22).

decisions.choice: the tax Moses laid on Israel in the wilderness: Exodus 30:12-16
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, this is the half-shekel each counted person paid for the service of the tent of meeting (Exodus 30:12-16). Now it is given "to Yahweh" again, for his house.

decisions.choice: slave of God (Literal); servant of God (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6. Here Moses is called the servant "of God" rather than "of Yahweh".

decisions.choice: that the people should bring
decisions.reason: Balanced names who was to bring the tax; the Hebrew leaves it general.

records.source: וַיִּשְׂמְח֥וּ כָל־הַשָּׂרִ֖ים וְכָל־הָעָ֑ם וַיָּבִ֛יאוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֥יכוּ לָאָר֖וֹן עַד־לְכַלֵּֽה׃
records.gloss: And rejoiced all the princes and all the people, and they brought and threw into the chest until finishing.
pieces: All the officials and all the people rejoiced. They brought their money and dropped it into the chest until they had finished.

L.10: And all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and they brought [it] and threw [it] into the chest until [they] finished.

R.10: All the leaders and all the people were glad to give. They brought their money and dropped it into the chest until they were done.

decisions.choice: they rejoiced: the people gave gladly
decisions.reason: Chronicles often marks giving to Yahweh's house with joy, as when the people gave for the first temple (1 Chronicles 29:9). Leaders and people alike take part.

decisions.choice: until finishing: until all had given, or until the chest was full
decisions.reason: The phrase is short: "until finishing". It most likely means until everyone had brought their gift; it may also mean until the chest was full, which leads into verse 11.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word for a ruler or official in these books.

decisions.choice: their money ... dropped it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves what they brought unstated; it is the tax of verse 9. "Were glad to give" at Readable says what their joy was about.

records.source: וַיְהִ֡י בְּעֵת֩ יָבִ֨יא אֶת־הָֽאָר֜וֹן אֶל־פְּקֻדַּ֣ת הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ בְּיַ֣ד הַלְוִיִּם֒ וְכִרְאוֹתָ֞ם כִּי־רַ֣ב הַכֶּ֗סֶף וּבָ֨א סוֹפֵ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וּפְקִיד֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הָרֹ֔אשׁ וִיעָ֨רוּ֙ אֶת־הָ֣אָר֔וֹן וְיִשָּׂאֻ֖הוּ וִֽישִׁיבֻ֣הוּ אֶל־מְקֹמ֑וֹ כֹּ֤ה עָשׂוּ֙ לְי֣וֹם׀בְּי֔וֹם וַיַּֽאַסְפוּ־כֶ֖סֶף לָרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] time [one] brought the chest to [the] oversight of the king by [the] hand of the Levites, and when they saw that much [was] the money, and came [the] scribe of the king and [the] officer of [the] priest the head, and they emptied the chest and carried it and returned it to its place; thus they did day by day, and they gathered money in abundance.
pieces: Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king's officials and they saw that it held a large sum of money, the king's secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, then carry it back to its place. They did this day after day and collected a great amount of money.

L.11: And it was, at the time [when] the chest was brought to the king's officers by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that the money [was] much, then the scribe of the king and the officer of the chief priest came and emptied the chest, and they carried it and returned it to its place. Thus they did day by day, and they gathered money in abundance.

R.11: From time to time the Levites brought the chest to the king's officials. When they saw that it held a lot of money, the king's secretary and the chief priest's officer came and emptied it. Then they carried the chest back to its place. They did this every day, and they collected a large amount of money.

decisions.choice: the king's scribe and the chief priest's officer: differs from 2 Kings 12:11
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 12:11 the king's scribe and "the high priest" himself come up and count the money. Here the chief priest sends his officer. In both accounts the palace and the temple handle the money together, so that it is counted openly.

decisions.choice: the king's scribe: the royal secretary
decisions.reason: The scribe was one of the king's chief officials, who kept records and handled royal business (2 Samuel 8:17; 1 Kings 4:3).

decisions.choice: the oversight of the king: the king's officers
decisions.reason: The word means oversight or charge, and here stands for the men the king had put in charge of the money.

decisions.choice: day by day: whenever there was need
decisions.reason: The emptying was done again and again, as often as the chest filled. "Day by day" stresses how often it happened.

decisions.choice: the king's secretary
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 12:11, Balanced and Readable say "secretary" for the royal scribe (m2); Literal keeps "scribe".

decisions.choice: short sentences in order of events
decisions.reason: Readable divides the long Hebrew sentence into four sentences in the order things were done.

records.source: וַיִּתְּנֵ֨הוּ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וִֽיהוֹיָדָ֗ע אֶל־עוֹשֵׂה֙ מְלֶ֨אכֶת֙ עֲבוֹדַ֣ת בֵּית־יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּֽהְי֤וּ שֹׂכְרִים֙ חֹצְבִ֣ים וְחָרָשִׁ֔ים לְחַדֵּ֖שׁ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְ֠גַם לְחָרָשֵׁ֤י בַרְזֶל֙ וּנְחֹ֔שֶׁת לְחַזֵּ֖ק אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And gave it the king and Jehoiada to [the] doer of [the] work of [the] service of [the] house of Yahweh, and they were hiring hewers and craftsmen to renew [the] house of Yahweh, and also to craftsmen of iron and bronze to repair the house of Yahweh.
pieces: The king and Jehoiada gave the money to those in charge of the work on the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they hired stonecutters and craftsmen to restore the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They also hired workers in iron and bronze to mend the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: And the king and Jehoiada gave it to the doer of the work of the service of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they were hiring hewers and craftsmen to renew the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and also craftsmen in iron and bronze to repair the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: The king and Jehoiada gave the money to the men in charge of the work on the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. These men hired stonecutters and skilled workers to restore the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They also hired people who worked with iron and bronze to repair the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the doer of the work: the overseers of the work
decisions.reason: The word is singular in form but stands for the men in charge of the work, who paid the workmen (2 Kings 12:12). Verse 13 uses the plural.

decisions.choice: hewers and craftsmen: stonecutters and skilled workers
decisions.reason: The first word is for those who cut or quarry stone. The second is a general word for a skilled craftsman, used with "of iron and bronze" for metalworkers; on its own here it most likely means workers in wood.

decisions.choice: workers in iron and bronze: not named in 2 Kings 12
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 12:12-13 names carpenters, builders, masons and stonecutters, and the purchase of timber and stone. Chronicles adds metalworkers, recalling the bronze work of Solomon's temple (2 Chronicles 4).

decisions.choice: restore ... mend (Balanced); restore ... repair (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has two verbs, "renew" and "repair" (verses 4-5); Balanced and Readable keep two different words.

decisions.choice: skilled workers
decisions.reason: Readable uses a general word, since the kind of craftsman is not stated (m2).

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה וַתַּ֧עַל אֲרוּכָ֛ה לַמְּלָאכָ֖ה בְּיָדָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲמִ֜ידוּ אֶת־בֵּ֧ית הָֽאֱלֹהִ֛ים עַל־מַתְכֻּנְתּ֖וֹ וַֽיְאַמְּצֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And worked [the] doers of the work, and went up healing for the work by their hand, and they set up [the] house of God on its measure and strengthened it.
pieces: So the workmen did their work, and the repairs went forward under their hands. They restored the house of God to its proper design and made it strong.

L.13: And the doers of the work worked, and healing went up for the work by their hand, and they set up the house of God according to its measure and strengthened it.

R.13: The workers did their job, and the repairs went well. They rebuilt God's temple as it was first planned, and they made it strong.

decisions.choice: healing went up: the repair advanced
decisions.reason: The word for repair is used of new flesh growing over a wound (Jeremiah 8:22; 30:17). The damaged house is pictured as being healed, and the healing "goes up", that is, makes progress.

decisions.choice: set up the house on its measure: restored it to its first plan
decisions.reason: The verb means to make stand. "Its measure" is the right size and design of the house, as Solomon built it. The work brought it back to that, and made it firm.

decisions.choice: the repairs went forward; the repairs went well
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture of healing means (m1); Literal keeps it.

records.source: וּֽכְכַלּוֹתָ֡ם הֵבִ֣יאוּ לִפְנֵי֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וִֽיהוֹיָדָ֜ע אֶת־שְׁאָ֣ר הַכֶּ֗סֶף וַיַּעֲשֵׂ֨הוּ כֵלִ֤ים לְבֵית־יְהוָה֙ כְּלֵ֣י שָׁרֵ֔ת וְהַעֲל֣וֹת וְכַפּ֔וֹת וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב וָכָ֑סֶף וַ֠יִּֽהְיוּ מַעֲלִ֨ים עֹל֤וֹת בְּבֵית־יְהוָה֙ תָּמִ֔יד כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹיָדָֽע׃פ
records.gloss: And when they finished they brought before the king and Jehoiada the rest of the money, and he made it vessels for [the] house of Yahweh, vessels of ministering and of offering up, and dishes and vessels of gold and silver; and they were offering up burnt offerings in [the] house of Yahweh continually all [the] days of Jehoiada.
pieces: When they had finished, they brought what remained of the money to the king and Jehoiada, and with it they made articles for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: articles for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and other articles of gold and silver. All the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were offered continually in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: And when they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, and it was made into vessels for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, vessels for ministering and for offering up, and dishes, and vessels of gold and silver. And they were offering up burnt offerings in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} continually all the days of Jehoiada.

R.14: When the work was finished, the workers brought the money that was left to the king and Jehoiada. It was used to make things for the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: objects for the temple service and for burnt offerings, dishes, and other things made of gold and silver. As long as Jehoiada lived, burnt offerings were offered in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} every day.

decisions.choice: the money left over made into vessels: compare 2 Kings 12:14
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 12:14 says that no gold or silver vessels were made from the money brought in. Kings speaks of the time the repairs were going on; Chronicles tells what was done with what remained once they were finished.

decisions.choice: vessels of ministering and of offering up; dishes
decisions.reason: These are the articles used in the temple service. "Offering up" is the verb used of burnt offerings, so these are vessels used with them. The dishes are small pans, used for incense (Numbers 7:14).

decisions.choice: continually, all the days of Jehoiada: regular worship while Jehoiada lived
decisions.reason: "Continually" is the word for the daily burnt offering, offered morning and evening (Numbers 28:3-6; 2 Chronicles 2:3). The phrase "all the days of Jehoiada" repeats verse 2 and prepares for what changes after his death (verse 17).

decisions.choice: he made it: it was made
decisions.reason: The verb is singular with no subject named; it means simply that the money was made into vessels.

decisions.choice: it was made into; they made; It was used to make
decisions.reason: Each level words the unnamed subject (m4) in its own way without naming who did the work.

decisions.choice: every day
decisions.reason: Readable says what "continually" means for the burnt offerings (m3).

records.source: וַיִּזְקַ֧ן יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע וַיִּשְׂבַּ֥ע יָמִ֖ים וַיָּמֹ֑ת בֶּן־מֵאָ֧ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה בְּמוֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And grew old Jehoiada and was satisfied [with] days and died; [a] son of a hundred and thirty years at his death.
pieces: Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and he died. He was 130 years old when he died.

L.15: And Jehoiada grew old and was full of days, and he died; a son of 130 years [was he] at his death.

R.15: Jehoiada lived to be very old, and he had a long, full life. He was 130 years old when he died.

decisions.choice: full of days: having lived a long and complete life
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Abraham, Isaac, David and Job (Genesis 25:8; 35:29; 1 Chronicles 29:28; Job 42:17). It describes a life lived to its full measure, with honor.

decisions.choice: 130 years: an age beyond Moses and Joshua
decisions.reason: Moses died at 120 and Joshua at 110 (Deuteronomy 34:7; Joshua 24:29). The great age marks Jehoiada as a man God honored.

decisions.choice: he had a long, full life
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1).

records.source: וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בְעִיר־דָּוִ֖יד עִם־הַמְּלָכִ֑ים כִּֽי־עָשָׂ֤ה טוֹבָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעִ֥ם הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וּבֵיתֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And they buried him in [the] city of David with the kings, for he had done good in Israel and with God and his house.
pieces: He was buried among the kings in the City of David, because of the good he had done in Israel for God and for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house.

L.16: And they buried him in the City of David with the kings, for he had done good in Israel, and with God and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house.

R.16: He was buried in the City of David with the kings, because he had done good things in Israel for God and for God's temple.

decisions.choice: buried with the kings: an honor given to a priest
decisions.reason: Jehoiada was not of the royal line, but he was given a place among the kings in the City of David. The honor stands in contrast with Joash, who is buried in the City of David but not in the tombs of the kings (verse 25).

decisions.choice: his house: the house of God
decisions.reason: "His" most naturally refers to God, the last one named; Jehoiada had restored the king and the worship of God's house (chapter 23; verses 12-14 here). It could be read as Jehoiada's own house, but that makes less sense in a reason for an honor.

decisions.choice: He was buried
decisions.reason: "They buried him" names no one in particular; Balanced and Readable say "was buried", as with the death formula.

decisions.choice: God's temple
decisions.reason: Readable names whose house it was (m2) instead of using a pronoun.

records.source: וְאַֽחֲרֵ֥י מוֹת֙ יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע בָּ֚אוּ שָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אָ֛ז שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And after [the] death of Jehoiada came [the] princes of Judah and bowed down to the king; then listened the king to them.
pieces: After Jehoiada's death the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king, and the king listened to them.

L.17: And after the death of Jehoiada the princes of Judah came and bowed down to the king; then the king listened to them.

R.17: After Jehoiada died, the leaders of Judah came and bowed low before the king. And the king listened to what they said.

decisions.choice: after Jehoiada's death the king listened to the princes
decisions.reason: The good years were tied to Jehoiada's life (verses 2, 14). Now other voices guide the king. The text does not say what they asked, but verse 18 shows where their advice led.

decisions.choice: bowed down to the king: a sign of honor, perhaps to win his favor
decisions.reason: Bowing low is the usual way of honoring a king. Coming just after Jehoiada's death and before a request, it suggests they were seeking the king's favor for their purpose.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

records.heading: Joash turns away; Zechariah is stoned

records.source: וַיַּֽעַזְב֗וּ אֶת־בֵּ֤ית יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּֽעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְאֶת־הָֽעֲצַבִּ֑ים וַֽיְהִי־קֶ֗צֶף עַל־יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּאַשְׁמָתָ֖ם זֹֽאת׃
records.gloss: And they forsook [the] house of Yahweh, [the] God of their fathers, and served the Asherahs and the idols; and was wrath on Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.
pieces: They forsook the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherah poles and the idols. Because of this guilt of theirs, wrath came on Judah and Jerusalem.

L.18: And they forsook the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherah poles and the idols; and wrath came on Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.

R.18: They abandoned the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors. They began to serve idols and the poles used to worship Asherah. Because they were guilty of this, God's anger came on Judah and Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: they forsook the house of Yahweh: the key word of the chapter
decisions.reason: The verb "forsake" returns in Zechariah's words (verse 20), in the reason for Judah's defeat (verse 24) and in the Arameans leaving the wounded king (verse 25). The house that Joash had restored is now abandoned. Chronicles uses the word for turning from Yahweh (12:1, 5; 15:2).

decisions.choice: the Asherahs and the idols
decisions.reason: The Asherahs were wooden poles or images standing for the goddess Asherah, set up at places of worship (Deuteronomy 16:21; 2 Chronicles 14:2). The second word is a general name for idols.

decisions.choice: wrath came: Yahweh's anger
decisions.reason: The text says only "wrath", but it is the anger of Yahweh at Judah's guilt, as elsewhere in Chronicles (19:2, 10; 1 Chronicles 27:24). Verses 23-24 show it at work.

decisions.choice: forsook (Literal, Balanced); abandoned (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use "forsake" for every use of this verb in the chapter, so the repeated word stays visible (m1); Readable uses the plainer "abandon" and "turn away".

decisions.choice: Asherah poles; poles used to worship Asherah
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books.

decisions.choice: God's anger
decisions.reason: Readable names whose wrath it was (m3).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח בָּהֶם֙ נְבִאִ֔ים לַהֲשִׁיבָ֖ם אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּעִ֥ידוּ בָ֖ם וְלֹ֥א הֶאֱזִֽינוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And he sent among them prophets to bring them back to Yahweh, and they testified against them, and not they gave ear.
pieces: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent prophets among them to bring them back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The prophets warned them, but they would not listen.

L.19: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent prophets among them to bring them back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they testified against them, but they did not give ear.

R.19: Even so, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent prophets to the people to bring them back to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The prophets warned them, but the people would not listen.

decisions.choice: he sent prophets: Yahweh's patience before judgment
decisions.reason: The one who sends is Yahweh. Before the wrath of verse 18 falls in full, he sends prophets to call the people back. Chronicles often tells of such warnings (36:15-16), and verse 20 gives one of them.

decisions.choice: testified against them: warned them solemnly
decisions.reason: The verb means to call as a witness, and so to warn someone with the weight of a witness behind the words, so that they are left without excuse.

decisions.choice: did not give ear: refused to listen
decisions.reason: To give ear is to listen and take heed. The people heard the prophets but would not obey.

decisions.choice: the LORD sent
decisions.reason: Readable names Yahweh as the one who sent (m1) and calls the people "the people" so the two groups are not confused.

records.source: וְר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֗ים לָֽבְשָׁה֙ אֶת־זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּן־יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד מֵעַ֣ל לָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים לָמָה֩ אַתֶּ֨ם עֹבְרִ֜ים אֶת־מִצְוֺ֤ת יְהוָה֙ וְלֹ֣א תַצְלִ֔יחוּ כִּֽי־עֲזַבְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וַיַּֽעֲזֹ֥ב אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, thus says God, why [are] you transgressing [the] commandments of Yahweh? And not you will prosper; for you have forsaken Yahweh, and he has forsaken you.
pieces: Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood up above the people and said to them, "God says this: 'Why do you break the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? You will not prosper. Because you have forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has forsaken you.'"

L.20: And the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, "Thus says God: 'Why are you transgressing the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? You will not prosper! Because you have forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has forsaken you.'"

R.20: Then the Spirit of God came on Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest and took hold of him. Zechariah stood where all the people could see him and said to them, "This is what God says: 'Why are you disobeying the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? You will not succeed. You have abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has abandoned you.'"

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah: took hold of him completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to put on clothes. The Spirit wraps Zechariah like a garment and speaks through him, as with Gideon and Amasai (Judges 6:34; 1 Chronicles 12:19). Zechariah is a priest, the son of Jehoiada, yet here he speaks as a prophet.

decisions.choice: stood above the people: on a raised place where all could see
decisions.reason: The words "from above" suggest he stood higher than the crowd, perhaps on a step or platform in the temple court (verse 21).

decisions.choice: because you have forsaken Yahweh, he has forsaken you
decisions.reason: The same verb is used both ways: as they have done to Yahweh, so he does to them. Shemaiah spoke the same words to Rehoboam (12:5), and Azariah warned Asa of it (15:2). It answers verse 18, "they forsook the house of Yahweh".

decisions.choice: you will not prosper: a statement of the outcome
decisions.reason: The words can be read as part of the question ("why ... so that you do not prosper?") or as a plain statement. Either way they warn that turning from Yahweh's commands brings failure (26:5; 1 Chronicles 22:13).

decisions.choice: Thus says God / God says this / This is what God says
decisions.reason: The messenger formula is worded at each level as in these books; here the speaker is named as God rather than Yahweh.

decisions.choice: came on Zechariah and took hold of him; stood where all the people could see him
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two pictures (m1, m2), as at 1 Chronicles 12:19. It also says "abandoned" for "forsaken", as in verse 18.

records.source: וַיִּקְשְׁר֣וּ עָלָ֔יו וַיִּרְגְּמֻ֥הוּ אֶ֖בֶן בְּמִצְוַ֣ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בַּחֲצַ֖ר בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they conspired against him and stoned him [with] stone at [the] command of the king in [the] court of [the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: But they plotted against him, and at the king's command they stoned him to death in the courtyard of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: And they conspired against him and stoned him [with] stone at the command of the king in the court of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: But the people plotted against Zechariah. At the king's order they threw stones at him until he died. They did this in the courtyard of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: in the court of the house of Yahweh: at the very temple
decisions.reason: The killing took place in the temple court, where Joash himself had been crowned under Jehoiada's protection (23:5, 10-11). Shedding innocent blood in a holy place made the crime all the worse.

decisions.choice: they conspired ... at the command of the king
decisions.reason: "They" are the people and their leaders who would not listen (verses 17-19). The plot is theirs, but the king gives the order and so bears the guilt (verse 22).

decisions.choice: stoned him to death; threw stones at him until he died
decisions.reason: Stoning was a way of putting someone to death, and verse 22 says Joash killed him. Balanced and Readable say so here.

decisions.choice: the people plotted against Zechariah
decisions.reason: Readable names who plotted and against whom (m2).

records.source: וְלֹא־זָכַ֞ר יוֹאָ֣שׁ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הַחֶ֨סֶד֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה יְהוֹיָדָ֤ע אָבִיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֖ג אֶת־בְּנ֑וֹ וּכְמוֹת֣וֹ אָמַ֔ר יֵ֥רֶא יְהוָ֖ה וְיִדְרֹֽשׁ׃פ
records.gloss: And not remembered Joash the king the loyalty which had done Jehoiada his father with him, and he killed his son; and as he died he said, may see Yahweh and may require.
pieces: King Joash did not remember the faithful love that Jehoiada, Zechariah's father, had shown him, and he killed his son. As Zechariah was dying, he said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} see this and call you to account!"

L.22: And Joash the king did not remember the steadfast love that Jehoiada his father had done with him, and he killed his son. And as he died he said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} see and require [it]!"

R.22: King Joash forgot the faithful love that Jehoiada, Zechariah's father, had shown him. He killed Jehoiada's son. As Zechariah was dying, he said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} see what you have done and make you pay for it!"

decisions.choice: the steadfast love Jehoiada had done him: loyal kindness
decisions.reason: Jehoiada had hidden Joash as a baby, made him king and guided him for years (22:11-12; 23:1-11). Joash repays that loyal love by killing Jehoiada's son. "Did not remember" means more than forgetting: he acted as though it had never been.

decisions.choice: his father ... his son: Jehoiada, Zechariah's father; Zechariah
decisions.reason: "His father" is the father of Zechariah, the man killed (verse 20), and "his son" is Jehoiada's son.

decisions.choice: may Yahweh see and require it: may he call the murderer to account
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or require. With bloodshed it means that God demands an account for a life taken (Genesis 9:5; 42:22). Zechariah's last words call on Yahweh as judge, as the blood of Abel cried out from the ground (Genesis 4:10). Verses 23-25 show the answer.

decisions.choice: Zechariah's death recalled by Jesus (Matthew 23:35; Luke 11:51)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the blood of the righteous from Abel to Zechariah, killed between the sanctuary and the altar. Abel's death is told at the start of the Hebrew Bible and Zechariah's in Chronicles, which often stands last in its order of books, so the two may mark its whole span. Matthew calls him the son of Barachiah, which has been explained in different ways.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books.

decisions.choice: Zechariah's father; As Zechariah was dying; call you to account / make you pay for it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Zechariah so the pronouns are clear (m2), and say what Yahweh is asked to require (m3). Literal keeps the bare verbs.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀לִתְקוּפַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה עָלָיו֮ חֵ֣יל אֲרָם֒ וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ אֶל־יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיַּשְׁחִ֛יתוּ אֶת־כָּל־שָׂרֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם מֵעָ֑ם וְכָל־שְׁלָלָ֥ם שִׁלְּח֖וּ לְמֶ֥לֶךְ דַּרְמָֽשֶׂק׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] turn of the year, came up against him [the] army of Aram, and they came to Judah and Jerusalem, and they destroyed all [the] princes of the people from [the] people, and all their plunder they sent to [the] king of Damascus.
pieces: At the turn of the year the army of Aram came up against Joash. They came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the officials of the people from among the people, and they sent all their plunder to the king of Damascus.

L.23: And it was at the turn of the year, the army of Aram came up against him, and they came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the princes of the people from the people, and all their plunder they sent to the king of Damascus.

R.23: At the turn of the year the Aramean army attacked Joash. They came into Judah and Jerusalem and killed all the leaders of the people. They sent everything they had taken to their king in Damascus.

decisions.choice: the turn of the year: the end of one year and start of the next
decisions.reason: The word means the circuit or turning point of the year. Exodus 34:22 uses it for the time of the autumn harvest feast. Here it gives a date, perhaps a year after Zechariah's death, without saying which season the writer counted from.

decisions.choice: all the princes of the people destroyed: the leaders who led the people astray
decisions.reason: The princes of Judah had turned the king to idols (verses 17-18). Now the princes are the ones destroyed. Judgment falls first on those who led the way.

decisions.choice: the army of Aram and the king of Damascus: Hazael's campaign (2 Kings 12:18-19)
decisions.reason: The king of Aram ruled from Damascus. 2 Kings 12:18-19 tells how Hazael king of Aram took Gath and turned toward Jerusalem, and Jehoash paid him off with the temple treasures. Chronicles tells of a battle and the loss of Judah's leaders, and does not name the Aramean king.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, so the reader sees that the same group is meant (m2).

decisions.choice: against Joash
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king for "him".

records.heading: The end of Joash's reign

records.source: כִּי֩ בְמִצְעַ֨ר אֲנָשִׁ֜ים בָּ֣אוּ׀חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֗ם וַֽיהוָה֙ נָתַ֨ן בְּיָדָ֥ם חַ֨יִל֙ לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י עָֽזְב֔וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֶת־יוֹאָ֖שׁ עָשׂ֥וּ שְׁפָטִֽים׃
records.gloss: For with [a] few of men came [the] army of Aram, and Yahweh gave into their hand an army for multitude very, for they had forsaken Yahweh, [the] God of their fathers; and with Joash they did judgments.
pieces: Though the army of Aram came with only a few men, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave a very great army into their power, because Judah had forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors. So they carried out judgment on Joash.

L.24: For with a few men the army of Aram came, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave into their hand a very great army, because they had forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers; and on Joash they executed judgments.

R.24: The Aramean army was small, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} let it defeat Judah's much larger army. This happened because the people of Judah had abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors. In this way the Arameans brought punishment on Joash.

decisions.choice: a few men defeat a great army: the reverse of Judah's earlier victories
decisions.reason: Under Abijah, Asa and Jehoshaphat, Yahweh gave Judah victory over far larger armies because they relied on him (13:3-18; 14:7-14; 20:12, 22-24). Now the same pattern is turned around: a small army wins because Judah has forsaken Yahweh.

decisions.choice: they had forsaken; they executed judgments: Judah, then the Arameans
decisions.reason: Those who "had forsaken" are Judah, the great army. Those who "executed judgments" on Joash are the Arameans, carrying out Yahweh's judgment. The plural "judgments" may mean acts of punishment.

decisions.choice: gave into their hand: put under their power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. Yahweh lets the Arameans overpower Judah.

decisions.choice: gave into their power (Balanced); let it defeat (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in these books, Balanced turns "hand" into "power" and Readable says what it meant (m3).

decisions.choice: Judah had forsaken; the Arameans brought punishment
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who had forsaken (m2), and Readable names the Arameans as the ones who carried out judgment.

records.source: וּבְלֶכְתָּ֣ם מִמֶּ֗נּוּ כִּֽי־עָזְב֣וּ אֹתוֹ֮ בְּמַחֲלוּיִ֣ם רַבִּים֒ הִתְקַשְּׁר֨וּ עָלָ֜יו עֲבָדָ֗יו בִּדְמֵי֙ בְּנֵי֙ יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וַיַּֽהַרְגֻ֥הוּ עַל־מִטָּת֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וְלֹ֥א קְבָרֻ֖הוּ בְּקִבְר֥וֹת הַמְּלָכִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And when they went from him, for they left him in many wounds, conspired against him his servants for [the] bloods of [the] sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed, and he died; and they buried him in [the] city of David, and not they buried him in [the] tombs of the kings.
pieces: When the Arameans withdrew, they left him badly wounded. His officials conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him in his bed. So he died. He was buried in the City of David, though not in the tombs of the kings.

L.25: And when they went away from him, for they left him with many wounds, his servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed, and he died. And they buried him in the City of David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.

R.25: When the Arameans left, Joash was badly wounded. His officials plotted against him because he had shed the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest. They killed him in his bed. He died. He was buried in the City of David, though not in the tombs where the kings lay.

decisions.choice: the sons of Jehoiada: plural in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "sons". Ancient Greek and Latin translations have "son", meaning Zechariah alone (verses 20-22). The plural may count other sons killed with him, or speak of the deed in general terms; it may also be an early copying slip. The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: killed on his bed; not buried in the tombs of the kings: differs from 2 Kings 12:21-22
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 12:21-22 says his servants struck him at Beth-millo and he was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and gives no reason. Chronicles says he was killed on his bed, gives the reason (the blood of Jehoiada's sons), and adds that he was not buried in the tombs of the kings. Jehoiada the priest was buried among the kings (verse 16); the king who killed his son was not.

decisions.choice: many wounds: badly hurt
decisions.reason: The word can mean sicknesses or wounds. Here, after the battle, he was left wounded and weak.

decisions.choice: they left him: the word "forsake" again
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for forsaking Yahweh (verses 18, 20, 24). Those who forsook Yahweh are forsaken; the king is left alone, wounded, to his own servants.

decisions.choice: left (every level); servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Here the verb means leaving a person behind, and every level says "left" (m4). The king's servants are "officials" at Balanced and Readable, as at 2 Kings 12:21.

decisions.choice: the Arameans; because he had shed the blood
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Arameans as the ones who withdrew, and Readable says whose deed the blood was.

records.source: וְאֵ֖לֶּה הַמִּתְקַשְּׁרִ֣ים עָלָ֑יו זָבָ֗ד בֶּן־שִׁמְעָת֙ הָֽעַמּוֹנִ֔ית וִיה֣וֹזָבָ֔ד בֶּן־שִׁמְרִ֖ית הַמּוֹאָבִֽית׃
records.gloss: And these [are] the ones conspiring against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonitess, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabitess.
pieces: These were the men who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.

L.26: And these [are] the ones conspiring against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.

R.26: The men who plotted against him were Zabad, whose mother was Shimeath, a woman from Ammon, and Jehozabad, whose mother was Shimrith, a woman from Moab.

decisions.choice: Zabad son of Shimeath, Jehozabad son of Shimrith: named a little differently in 2 Kings 12:22
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 12:22 calls them Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer. Zabad is a short form of Jozabad, and Shimrith is a feminine form of Shomer. Chronicles names the men by their mothers, and says the mothers were an Ammonite and a Moabite.

decisions.choice: the Ammonite woman, the Moabite woman: mothers from foreign nations
decisions.reason: Ammon and Moab were neighbors east of the Jordan and often enemies of Judah (20:1). Naming the killers' mothers this way may hint that the king who turned to foreign gods was brought down by men of foreign mothers, but the text only gives the facts.

decisions.choice: whose mother was
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the women named are the men's mothers.

records.source: וּבָנָ֞יו יִ֧רֶ֞ב הַמַּשָּׂ֣א עָלָ֗יו וִיסוֹד֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל־מִדְרַ֖שׁ סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֑ים וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And his sons, and [the] greatness of the oracle against him, and [the] founding of [the] house of God, look, they [are] written on [the] midrash of [the] book of the kings; and reigned Amaziah his son in his place.
pieces: The account of his sons, the many oracles against him, and the rebuilding of the house of God are written in the commentary on the Book of the Kings. And his son Amaziah became king in his place.

L.27: And his sons, and the many oracles against him, and the founding of the house of God, look, they [are] written in the midrash of the book of the kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

R.27: What happened to his sons, the many prophecies spoken against him, and how he rebuilt God's temple are all written in the commentary on the book of the kings. His son Amaziah became king after him.

decisions.choice: the midrash of the book of the kings: a written study or account of the kings
alternatives: the story of the book of the kings
the annotations on the book of the kings
decisions.reason: As at 13:22, the only other use of the word: a written work that searched out or set out the history, here of the kings, perhaps a commentary on an older record. It need not mean the later Jewish writings that carry the same name. The work has not survived.

decisions.choice: the many oracles against him
alternatives: the great tribute laid on him
decisions.reason: The word can mean an oracle, a message from God (as in verses 19-20), or a burden laid on someone, such as a tax or tribute. Read the first way, the record tells of the many prophecies against Joash; read the second, of the heavy tribute laid on him (compare 2 Kings 12:19). The Hebrew of the phrase is also unsettled between the written and the read forms.

decisions.choice: the founding of the house of God: its restoration
decisions.reason: "Founding" here means the work of building up again, the repairs of verses 4-14.

decisions.choice: look, they are written: a statement, not a question
decisions.reason: Here Chronicles does not use the question "are they not written?" but says directly that these things are written.

decisions.choice: midrash (Literal); the commentary on the Book of the Kings (Balanced); the commentary on the book of the kings (Readable)
decisions.reason: Worded as at 13:22: Literal keeps the Hebrew word, Balanced and Readable say "commentary". The book it comments on is written as a title at Balanced, as with the other source books of Chronicles (16:11), and plainly at Readable.

decisions.choice: Amaziah his son reigned in his place; became king in his place; became king after him
decisions.reason: Worded as at 2 Kings 12:22.
